lines.c1: Most studies ask how much faster AI makes developers.
lines.c2: We asked something different. What does AI let them do that they couldn't do before?
lines.c3: We put that question to three hundred and thirty-one developers at Microsoft.
lines.c4: Their answers fell into three zones.
lines.c5: Faster. The same work, done faster.
lines.c6: Further. Work that was once out of reach, or too costly to justify.
lines.c7: And Afresh. New kinds of work, built around AI.
lines.c8: Underneath all three is a loop. Developers and AI are joint learners.
lines.c9: Developers learn with AI's scaffolding. And AI learns from what developers codify: specs, memory, and success criteria.
lines.c10: With each turn of the loop, what both can do moves outward.
lines.c11: They meet at the skill-judgment nexus. AI can supply skill faster than it can judge its own work, so developers bridge the gap.
lines.c12: But when skill outpaces judgment, the loop stalls. Over-dependence, a growing verification burden, and an erosion of skill and identity.
lines.c13: To keep it turning, we offer a two-way scaffolding playbook.
lines.c14: Practices for before, during, and after the work, flowing from developer to AI, and from AI to developer.
